identity.description: Neo4j, the graph database company and its graph database platform (Neo4j Aura cloud service, Cypher query language, Neo4j drivers). The assignment's neo4j.com/docs/api path redirects to the Aura API docs (neo4j.com/docs/aura/current/api/...); there is no separate general 'Neo4j API' page found.
identity.identity_notes: Sources clearly describe the Neo4j graph database product. The 'neo4j.com/docs/api' hint is a general path; the substantive API docs are the Aura API (cloud management) plus the HTTP Query API and Bolt drivers (database access).

auth.oauth_flows: Aura API: OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant. POST to https://api.neo4j.io/oauth/token with grant_type=client_credentials; client ID/secret sent via HTTP Basic auth. Returned bearer token used in Authorization header.
auth.token_refresh: Access tokens expire after one hour; request a new token via the same client_credentials exchange. Client credentials do not expire unless deleted.
auth.scopes_notes: No scopes described in fetched sources. Aura API credentials are per-client ID/secret pairs created in the console.

access.production_restrictions: No app review found. Docs say all tiers can create Aura API credentials, but a community thread reports Free/Professional users must add billing info or join a marketplace project to create API credentials, and Aura API rate limits apply to Free/Professional trial accounts without a billing method (25 req/min). Treat as free self-serve with a possible billing gate; verify in console.

write_ops: Instance actions (create/update/delete not confirmed from fetched pages beyond 'perform actions on your Aura instances')
api.rate_limits: 25 requests/min for AuraDB Free and Professional trial accounts without billing method; billing endpoints 10 requests/day per org; 45-second request timeout; excessive token requests may be rate-limited.
api.limitations: Aura management API covers instances per fetched overview; full endpoint list is in a separate API Specification not fetched. Database data access uses the HTTP Query API (REST, Basic/Bearer auth) and Bolt drivers (binary protocol, not in enum) for Cypher queries; those were not fully enumerated. Webhooks not mentioned in fetched docs. Python driver API reference exists (search snippet only, not fetched).
